question.text: A <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5000</mn><mo> </mo><mo>kg</mo></math> rocket is set for vertical firing. The exhaust speed is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>800</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. To give an initial upward acceleration of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> m</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>s</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></math> what is the amount of gas ejected (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>) to supply the needed thrust? (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> m</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>s</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
Given : Mass of rocket (m)=5000 Kg

Exhaust speed (v)=800 m s-1

Acceleration of rocket (a)=20 m s-2

Gravitational acceleration (g)=10 m s-2

We know that upward force

F=m(g+a)=5000(10+20)

=5000×30=150000 N

We also know that amount of gas ejected

(dmdt)=Fv=150000800=187.5 kg s-1
